items.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023
items.q: he was basically conducting for Milton Berle and Anthony Newley and Donald O’Connor

ctx.x: Last question. Of all the things you’ve done from going into clubs and sitting in to standing in front of a 60-piece orchestra, is there a through line through that? Is there something that is always a constant for you?

Gee. I mean I’m just totally enamored of making music in some way. So to stand in front of my quartet and play, “I Wish I Knew” or an obscure standard is just as exciting as doing a downbeat in front of the London Symphony Orchestra. It’s a different excitement I guess. But it’s still an extension of exactly where I was when I started, which not a lot of people can say that. The one thing that — when I saw my uncle a lot when he moved to America and I was in America, and he was basically conducting for Milton…
I’d like to think that that’s important, that you’re still connected in a physical way to the players who are making your music come alive, and you still know what that feels like.
